title: RAGing Against Misogyny: Improving Implicit Misogyny Explanations
abstract: arXiv:2610.35094v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Implicit misogyny often requires background knowledge to be understood. To address this challenge, we propose a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for detecting and explaining implicit misogyny in English and Italian, leveraging encyclopedic, slang and feminist knowledge sources. Using the ImplicIT-Mis and SBIC+ datasets, we evaluate the contribution of each knowledge source to detection and explanation quality, investigating also whether RAG addresses known LLM failure modes in implicit misogyny. Results show that RAG improves recall on ImplicIT-Mis, but does not improve detection performance on SBIC+. However, human evaluation shows that RAG-based explanations are preferred over no-RAG explanations in both languages. Feminist literature emerges as the most consistently useful source for detection and explanation.

translated_title: 以RAG对抗厌女：改进隐性厌女言论的解释
translated_abstract: 隐性厌女言论通常需要背景知识才能被理解。为了应对这一挑战，我们提出了一个检索增强生成（RAG）框架，用于检测和解释英语和意大利语中的隐性厌女言论，该框架利用了百科知识、俚语知识和女性主义知识来源。基于ImplicIT-Mis和SBIC+数据集，我们评估了每种知识来源对检测和解释质量的贡献，并研究了RAG是否能解决大语言模型在处理隐性厌女言论时的已知失败模式。结果表明，RAG提高了在ImplicIT-Mis上的召回率，但在SBIC+上并未提升检测性能。然而，人类评估显示，在两种语言中，基于RAG生成的解释都比不使用RAG的解释更受青睐。女性主义文献被证明是对检测和解释最持续有用的知识来源。
tldr: 本研究提出利用检索增强生成（RAG）框架，结合百科、俚语和女性主义知识来源，改进英语和意大利语中隐性厌女言论的检测与解释，其中女性主义文献被证明是最持续有用的知识来源。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a RAG framework leveraging encyclopedic, slang, and feminist knowledge sources to improve detection and explanation of implicit misogyny in English and Italian, finding that feminist literature is the most consistently useful knowledge source.
